searchText: > all this complicated description does is tries to describe padding to 32*2^K bytes, in a complicated way 🙂 SSZ isn't just that, it also describes how to Merkle-hash compound structures, which code hashing needs because you would also want to have a top-level slice that includes the keccak code hash and some other metadata Having a well thought out data structure on top of which you get native merklization is way easier to work with than a trie structure that you put data into in order to get a merkle hash. exactly I have updated by understanding of SSZ and my views are different now More positive or more negative? I just understood where it could be useful to have such scheme. In the cases where you want (for some reasons that also need to be looked into) to construct merkle trees from heterogeneous things, and not only from byte strings. In our example, it is putting metadata somewhere along the code chunks I did not completely review SSZ merklelisation rules to check whether it introduces any problematic issues for non-opinionated implementations

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content:
> all this complicated description does is tries to describe padding to 32*2^K bytes, in a complicated way 🙂

SSZ isn't just that, it also describes how to Merkle-hash compound structures, which code hashing needs because you would also want to have a top-level slice that includes the keccak code hash and some other metadata

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: Having a well thought out data structure on top of which you get native merklization is way easier to work with than a trie structure that you put data into in order to get a merkle hash.
